name: MASTER
aliases: Male synthetic sling versus Artificial urinary Sphincter Trial: Evaluation by Randomised controlled trial
question: Is a fixed transobturator male sling noninferior to an artificial urinary sphincter for continence after prostate surgery?

design.population: Men at 27 UK centers with bothersome urodynamic stress urinary incontinence after prostate surgery, despite conservative treatment, who chose surgery and could receive either implant.
design.locator: Abrams 2021 PDF pp 813–815, Methods and Figure 1

verdictNote: Strict leakage endpoint met the margin; symptom scores and satisfaction favored AUS.
takeaway: In men undergoing surgery for stress incontinence after prostate surgery, a fixed transobturator synthetic sling met the 15-percentage-point noninferiority margin versus an artificial urinary sphincter for strict patient-reported continence at 12 months; symptom scores favored the sphincter.

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.citation: Abrams P, Constable LD, Cooper D, et al. Outcomes of a Noninferiority Randomised Controlled Trial of Surgery for Men with Urodynamic Stress Incontinence After Prostate Surgery (MASTER). *Eur Urol.* 2021;79(6):812-823. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2021.01.024
reports.followUp: Primary continence assessment at 12 months after randomization; adverse events through 12 months after surgery

results.measure: 12-month continent proportion; adjusted risk difference in percentage points (sling minus AUS)
results.note: Any leakage on either ICIQ-UI SF frequency or amount item counted as incontinence; prespecified continence risk-difference margin was -15 percentage points. The article abstract gives the difference with the opposite sign; Results/Table 2 use -3.6.

results.measure: 12-month score; adjusted mean difference in points (sling minus AUS)
results.note: Lower score indicates fewer symptoms; the 2022 full report gives a slightly different adjusted estimate.

results.measure: 12-month completely or fairly satisfied proportion; risk difference in percentage points (sling minus AUS)
results.note: Denominators reconstructed from the reported counts and percentages; the full HTA Table 11 separates satisfaction categories.
results.locator: PDF p 816, Satisfaction; HTA PDF p 59, Table 11

harms.label: Inpatient serious adverse events
harms.locator: PDF pp 817–819, Surgery and AEs; p 819, Table 3
harms.note: Three AUS events occurred in one man. Sling events included recatheterization (3), mesh erosion (1), urosepsis (1), and coffee-ground vomit (1); AUS events included recatheterization (3), infection (3), and device erosion (2).

harms.label: Catheter problems during admission
harms.locator: PDF p 817, Surgery and AEs; p 819, Table 3
harms.note: More common after sling; reported difference 17.5 percentage points (95% CI 10.0–24.9).

delivery.label: Treatment received by randomized group
delivery.note: Intention-to-treat analyses retained randomized assignment. The 2022 full report includes two additional AUS-arm operations.

delivery.label: Readmissions for further or additional surgery within 12 months
delivery.note: Twelve sling-arm men received AUS and one a second sling; three AUS-arm men had device revision. The AUS Table 4 separates further surgery (2) and additional surgery (1).

reports.citation: Constable L, Abrams P, Cooper D, et al. Synthetic sling or artificial urinary sphincter for men with urodynamic stress incontinence after prostate surgery: the MASTER non-inferiority RCT. *Health Technol Assess.* 2022;26(36):1-152. doi:10.3310/TBFZ0277

results.measure: 12-month score; adjusted mean difference in points (sling minus AUS)
results.note: Full-report estimate of the secondary symptom comparison already reported in the primary article.

results.measure: 24-month continent proportion; adjusted risk difference in percentage points (sling minus AUS)
results.note: Prespecified primary assessment was at 12 months; this later assessment used the same strict composite and -15-point margin.

results.measure: 24-month continent proportion; adjusted risk difference in percentage points (sling minus AUS)
results.note: Allows leakage once weekly or less and a small amount; confidence interval crosses the -15-point margin, and p exceeds the 0.025 one-sided threshold.
results.locator: HTA PDF p 53, Table 7 and footnote

results.measure: 24-month score; adjusted mean difference in points (sling minus AUS)
24-month mean cost; adjusted mean difference in pounds sterling (sling minus AUS)
results.note: Economic base case; sling had 0.006 fewer estimated quality-adjusted life-years, with 95% CI -0.06 to 0.054.
results.locator: HTA PDF pp 75–76, Table 19 and economic summary

harms.label: Inpatient serious adverse events in full report
harms.locator: HTA PDF pp 49–50, Table 6 and Adverse events
harms.note: The full report counts three sling mesh erosions versus one in the 2021 article; one AUS patient had three serious events. These are surgical-period events, not the 24-month patient-reported complications.

harms.label: Postoperative catheter required
harms.note: Catheterization longer than 24 hours occurred in 20/180 (11.1%) versus 6/175 (3.4%).

harms.label: Patient-reported surgical-site pain by 24 months
harms.note: Cumulative questionnaire reports; the table also lists urinary tract infection in 23/190 (12.1%) versus 20/190 (10.5%).

delivery.label: Operative technique
delivery.value: Nonadjustable polypropylene suburethral sling passed bilaterally through the obturator foramina; AUS urethral cuff, scrotal pump, and pressure-regulating balloon, left deactivated for 4–6 weeks before clinic activation.

delivery.label: Surgery received and crossover
delivery.note: Two more AUS-arm operations are counted here than in the 2021 article.

delivery.label: Further surgery through 24 months
delivery.locator: HTA PDF pp 26, 48–49, Scientific summary and Table 5
delivery.note: Eighteen sling-arm men received AUS and two a new sling; three AUS-arm men received a new AUS and one had removal without replacement.
